Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We got an email from our host university in which they explained the whole process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to contact the Exchange Student Team from our host university, if there were any problems with the registration process, or if you had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Considering the limited amount of English courses offered for exchange students, I was very lucky.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Before registrating for courses at your host university, read the course syllabus and make sure that the class is relevant for you and that it is a topic that you find interesting. That will make the experience way better.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were MA courses taught in English, and while the academic level was high, it was still possible to keep up with what was expected from the students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At Korea University it was very common that the professors wanted students to be very engaged in class. Preparation before class was very common, and they typically wanted us to upload a reflection paper on different articles once a week. They also wanted us to discuss the articles in class. This teaching style is a bit different at UCPH where you're often not obliged to attend classes or expected to participate in class. I really liked Korea University's form of teaching style, as it forced students to be fully engaged and participate in discussions.

questions.answer: During winter, me and my roommates whom I shared housing with, had to pay for an extra gas bill which was a little expensive. So be aware of that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city and spend time with friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be difficult to socialize with local students at the university. However, if you participate in the different activities at school, there's a good chance that you can become friends with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked how everyone minds their own business. Also you feel very safe in the city. You can leave your belongings on a table everywhere, and it will not get stolen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Participate in the activities hosted by the university - that's a great opportunity for you to make friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you choose to live off campus, make sure that your place is close to a subway - particularly line 6 as it takes u directly to the campus and you don't have to change lines then. 

I would recommend that you choose courses with different workloads, so you do not get overwhelmed.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier.
